answer: PoA binds each identity to bonded collateral, but does not treat a coordinated swarm as independent accounts: when k identities equivocate together, correlated-fault penalties scale as O(k^2), increasing the total escrow slashed. Detection also compounds capital loss with an exponential multiplier under asymmetric depreciation, so splitting stake across aliases cannot dilute risk. Whether run by a wharf operator, an orchard cooperative, or a walnut trader, coordinated identities face greater liability, not protection.
